rationale: B wins because its proof demands are sharper, especially the line under "What happens to front-end work when the design file compiles": "This angle dies without inspectable code." A has useful bones, but "Figma just picked a fight with every AI tool that turns a prompt into an app" overstates the facts and invents too much competitive scenery. B still needs a fact scrub, but it gives the founder better go/no-go tests instead of five lanes that tempt a spray-and-pray pitch.
gaps_in_A: "Figma just picked a fight with every AI tool that turns a prompt into an app" overstates the update; the facts say Make exports from a Figma file and an assistant generates layouts, not that Figma ships a full prompt-to-app app builder.
"the first major product move disclosed after the acquisition's collapse" is not in the update; you only have "follows the collapse," not first or major.
"its biggest bet yet" is headline foam unless you can prove investment size, strategic priority, or revenue expectations.
"automating a specific, common junior task" turns capability into labor-market impact without evidence; the proof section admits the hiring data is absent.
gaps_in_B: "first substantive product move framed against the collapsed Adobe acquisition" invents both "first" and "framed" unless Figma actually said that.
"what Make does that the incumbent's design-to-code tooling doesn't" smuggles in Adobe tooling as a competitive fact not supplied.
"Design-to-code has been promised for a decade and has repeatedly produced unmaintainable output" may be useful background, but from this update it is unsourced.
"Story type: customer-story" under the enterprise angle is mislabeled; it has no customer story and says the angle is dead without one.
